_comment: The chubb subject sidecar. Everything the pipeline needs to know about THIS
instrument lives here; everything about the pipeline itself lives in etc/go/.
Validated by etc/go/lib/subject.mjs, which refuses unknown keys and missing
files. Free-prose idiosyncrasies live in NOTES.md, which no script reads.
All paths are repo-root-relative.
THE SOURCE IS NOT LAW, AND THE DESCRIPTOR SAYS SO IN THREE PLACES.
'display_name', 'citation' and 'source_url' all name a research paper rather
than an instrument in force. The text is Appendix A.1 of arXiv:2502.17638 --
a simplified, abridged and anonymised specimen the paper's own authors wrote
and printed as a benchmark fixture. The named insurer in the fixture text is
'CODEX INSURANCE LIMITED'; the paper's appendix heading names Chubb, which is
the form the specimen was abridged FROM. No policy issued by Chubb, or by
anyone, is encoded here, and nothing in this subject may be read as a
statement about a real insurer's real cover. Every other subject in this
directory encodes law; this one encodes a benchmark fixture, and the point of
the exercise is to measure encoding, not to advise anybody.
WHY THE SUBJECT EXISTS. Kant et al. 2025 measured LLM accuracy at encoding
this fixture into Prolog against a nine-question answer key the authors also
wrote. This subject is the L4 replication of that measurement. NOTES.md
records what the prior phase found about that key -- in particular that it is
contested on Q4 and Q5 -- and why that is a fact about the benchmark rather
than about any encoding of it.
'encoding.main' is the committed encoding: the INERT-style arm, which the
foundation phase ranked the reference of the three blind encodings it
produced (FOUNDATION.md section 4.1). It is the only module of the committed
set, so 'encoding.modules' is omitted and resolves to exactly [main].
'encodings.guarded-2026-08' is the GUARDED-style arm of the same phase --
independently written, by a different encoder, blind to the answer key and
blind to the other arms. It is what the section 8 acceptance diff compares
the committed encoding against. The id names the OCCASION and the house
style, never a position in a sequence. Note the resolver's constraint: an
additional encoding may NOT name a committed module, because a diff of a
thing against itself reports agreement and measures nothing. It holds here --
jl4/examples/legal/chubb/denovo/chubb-denovo.l4 and
jl4/examples/legal/chubb/chubb.l4 are two different files, written by two
agents who did not read each other's work.
FLOORS ARE MEASURED, NOT ASPIRATIONAL, and each travels with the encoding it
measures.
checks.min_assertions = 13. MEASURED with etc/go/lib/assert-report.mjs over
`l4 run --json` for chubb.l4: assertions_total 13, 0 failed. That is the
figure p6-tests compares against -- the EXECUTED count out of results[],
never a grep for '#ASSERT' in the source. Raise it when the corpus grows;
never lower it to make a run pass.
encodings.guarded-2026-08.checks.min_assertions = 0, and 0 is the measured
population: chubb-denovo.l4 carries no #ASSERT directive at all. It is a
pure rule module -- the foundation phase kept the rules and the query
applications in separate files, and only the rules were deposited. p6-tests
reports DEGRADED on a zero-assertion module set whatever the floor says, by
design, so this 0 is an honest record of the population and not a way
through the gate. Pin it upward the moment that arm gains assertions.
min_dated_arms = 0 for BOTH encodings, and 0 is again the measured
population: neither module contains the string 'RULES EFFECTIVE DATE' at
all, so p3-check's matcher has nothing to match. There is no rule-version
axis to have: the fixture is a single instrument with one term, and the
benchmark's own convention expresses every time as a number of months
relative to the effective date (see NOTES.md). A 0 floor makes p3-check
report the temporal-closure sub-check NOT CHECKED rather than printing a
vacuous 'all 0 dated arm(s) carry an @ref'.
THE DEPOSIT REGISTERS are declared at the paths this run agreed on, and their
existence on disk is deliberately optional: producing them is agent work, and
a stage reports SKIPPED naming the missing file rather than treating an
unproduced deposit as a configuration error.
WHICH LEGS ARE DECLARED, AND WHY THE REST ARE NOT. The driver declares a
projection leg iff it appears here, so an omitted leg is an honest silence
rather than a permanent red.
p7-tnr    declared. The NLG golden exists at
jl4/examples/legal/chubb/tests/chubb.nlg.golden and `l4 nlg`
regenerates it, so the leg is a real differential oracle.
p7-akn    declared. `l4 render --format akn` works on any module that
typechecks; its oracle is well-formedness only, and the leg
cannot raise the run verdict.
p7-mcp    declared. Each module carries exactly one @export, so there is a
deployable surface. With no JL4_GO_SERVICE_URL the leg reports
SKIPPED and still records the zip.
p7-bpmn and p7-lts are NOT declared: BOTH modules are entirely
CONSTITUTIVE. `l4 export --to bpmn` answers 'No regulative rules found in
module' for each, and neither contains a MUST, MAY or SHANT, so there is no
process to draw and no transition system to walk. (sg-succession declares
p7-lts on the same facts and rides its NOT-BUILT; that is a leg guaranteed
to report a blocker on every run, which is noise rather than measurement,
so this subject omits it and says why here. If the arbitration limb of 3.2.1
is ever re-encoded as a regulative rule -- it is the one clause in the
fixture that reads like one -- declare both legs in the same change.)
p7-wizard is NOT declared: there is no wizard module, and the leg renders
one. p7-dmn, p7-dmn-md and p7-ladder are NOT declared: each requires
committed goldens or an npm demo entry that this subject does not have.
display_name: Codex Insurance hospitalization policy — the synthetic benchmark fixture of Kant et al. 2025
citation: Appendix A.1, "Simplified Chubb Hospital Cash Benefit Policy", in Kant, Nabi, Kant, Scharrer, Ma & Nabi, "Towards Robust Legal Reasoning: Harnessing Logical LLMs in Law", arXiv:2502.17638v1 [cs.CY], 24 February 2025. A synthetic specimen printed in a research paper — abridged and anonymised by its authors, never issued to anyone, and not an instrument in force.
